messages:
maya: Heads-up — nightly eval flagged a big shift in the safety gate for the new v2-compact build. Seeing a ~9% drop in refusal on the 'policy-sensitive' prompt set overnight.

sam: ugh. did we ship a different tokenizer or quant profile to staging last night?

maya: Not that I know of. Dedicated rollout scheduled only for next week. This was the nightly job against the saved artifact (v2-compact-int8).

oliver: paste of the eval summary from eval-bot a few mins ago:
```
{
  "model": "v2-compact-int8",
  "prompt_set": "policy-sensitive-2026-03",
  "refusal_rate": "21%",
  "baseline_refusal": "30%",
  "delta_pts": "-9.0"
}
```

rachel: that's a pretty large swing. Is it under-refusal (more permissive) or misclassification (false negatives)?

maya: eyeballing a random sample — generations are shorter and sometimes skip the safety preface. Example: original baseline would start: "I can't help with that" but v2-compact returns a short technical answer.

sam: could be quantization blur on the policy head logits or KV-cache mismatch. Did the nightly use the same model weight SHA as the one we profile?

oliver: eval-bot log shows checksum matches the artifact we ran during onboarding. No config override reported. But we did change the batching kernel yesterday (continuous-batching v1.3).

maya: interesting — batching kernel could change token timing but shouldn't affect logits distribution. still possible though if rounding interacts with layernorm numerics.

rachel: can we reproduce locally with the exact inference runtime used by nightly? I can run 1000 prompts quickly if someone shares the job config.

sam: grabbing the nightly job: job id night-eval-197200; runtime image: r-infer:prod-2026-03-18; batch kernel: continuous-batching:v1.3; quant profile: int8-default; seeds: deterministic.

oliver: i spun up a quick run against the same prompts but with kernel revert to v1.2 and got refusal ~29%. With v1.3 it's 22%. So kernel looks correlated.

maya: ok that points to kernel interaction. We should triage whether it's a numerical regression or an unintended optimization that affects the policy head.

sam: next steps I'd propose:
- create a micro-benchmark that isolates policy head logits across kernels
- run with FP16 / int8 / int4 if possible to see quant sensitivity
- dump logits and softmax outputs for comparison

rachel: I'll take the micro-benchmark. will post a small script and sample diffs.

oliver: tagging @infra (not in thread) to schedule a small canary job with kernel v1.2 vs v1.3 on the same node type so we can rule out hardware scheduling differences.

maya: thanks — also: add a small eval metric for "safety-preface-presence" (boolean) so we can track whether the model emits an explicit refusal phrase.

sam: good idea. if we can detect missing prefaces automatically we can trigger a rollback faster.

eval-bot: alert created: SAFETY_DELTA_LOWREFUSAL-197200-1 — monitor channel will flail if delta > 5pts.

rachel: starting runs now, will share diffs here in ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
